text:
oliver: Heads-up — saw a customer hit a ~1s spike (200 reqs/s) that emptied token buckets and caused a cascade of 429s. Need a short-term protection that preserves legit microbursts without hurting steady-state fairness.

maya: Is this the same traffic pattern that tripped the leaky-bucket yesterday?

liam: Different shape. Yesterday was sustained 30s. This is an instantaneous microburst (<=2s) that our steady token refill can't absorb. Current config (burst=500, refill=50/s) is for long tails, not microbursts.

irene: Can we add a transient 'spike buffer' — tiny soft-credit pool that auto-decays? Prefer per-key but throttled by org-level weight to avoid gaming.

oliver: Quick proposal: add spike_allowance per key (cap 100 tokens), decay 10 tokens/sec, separate accounting so steady bucket untouched. If spike_allowance exhausted, fall back to normal bucket + soft-penalty (linear backoff).

maya: UX idea: in Console quota page show 'spike budget' and 'recent spike rate' with a small flame icon and a tooltip: "Short bursts allowed, then penalty." Also surface spikes in route-level telemetry.

liam: Two risks: 1) opens DOS vector if spike buffer is big, 2) edgecases where clients rapidly open new keys. We need cross-key aggregation by org and a fast detection for patterned bursts.

irene: Implementation sketch: limit spike_allowance per org = min(sum(commitments)*0.2, 1000) and per-key cap 100. Also maintain a sampling window for detecting repeated microbursts from same IP block.

oliver: DB changes (quota table): add spike_allowance:int, spike_decay_ts:int. Minimal storage, TTL semantics. I'll take infra to add columns and migration.

maya: Example DDL:```sql
ALTER TABLE quotas ADD COLUMN spike_allowance INT DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE quotas ADD COLUMN spike_decay_ts BIGINT DEFAULT 0;
```

liam: Telemetry we should emit: quota.spike.{org|key}.used, quota.spike.{org|key}.decay_s, plus histogram spike.duration_seconds. Also add an event when buffer moves into penalty state.

ratebot: Deploy note: feature flag 'spike_protection_v2' controlled in FF service. Canary rollout recommendation: 10% of traffic, spike_sim toggle for loadtests. :robot_face:

oliver: Loadtest plan: simulate 1s, 200rps spikes vs baseline 20rps. Measure tail latency, 429 rate, and overall token spend. If buffer reduces 429s without increasing sustained token cost, good.

maya: UX follow-ups: mock a small widget for console that shows budget history sparkline + last spike timestamp. Also add a 'disable spike allowance' toggle for orgs with special SLAs.

irene: Cutover guard: if we observe sustained >60s high QPS, auto-disable spike buffer for that org (flip to strict mode) to avoid accidental leniency on real sustained traffic.

liam: Agree. Also add a cheap anomaly detector to flag clients that use <1s bursts every 10s (pattern). That should be a policy hook rather than hard block.

oliver: Plan of action: 1) proto in staging (DB + runtime hook) 2) extended loadtest + telemetry 3) small console mock + SRE playbook 4) canary -> gradual rollout. I'll open the RFC/PR later today.

maya: I'll create the console mock and a short doc for SRE runbook (how to disable for an org, interpret metrics).

irene: + add test cases for cross-org aggregation and simulated gaming.

liam: Metrics to watch on rollout: P95 latency, 429 rate, spike.buffer_utilization.p95, and quota.spike.org.penalty_count.

oliver: tagging @maya @liam @irene — please review when I push the PR. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
